R6F-bear-backcountry-0003.name: By Crag Creek
R6F-bear-backcountry-0003.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R6F-bear-backcountry-0003.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed paved road

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2010 (16 years old), 140 m W: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2023 (fire VA1638), 220 m E: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
W facing slope, 16 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Crag Creek 20 m SW: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

seasonRows.notes: Bag 2; parts of MU 5-9 are closed to black bear hunting (Map F14, page 52) and the Mussel Inlet Special Management Area in MU 5-9 has no black bear season (page 43)

plan: Drive: from Village of Burns Lake, about 226 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 52.78098, -126.6449, pull off on an unnamed paved road. Map links below.
Walk: 14 km SE, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 1,442 m, about 429 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 540 m N of the spot at 417 m (52.73128, -126.45625). Water: Crag Creek 40 m W (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 5-9, Region 5. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-02, closures 2026-10-16.
R6F-bear-backcountry-0003.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 5-9: about 36 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.00 days per square km, bottom third of BC MUs; access: more than 5 km from a drivable road. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

R6F-deer-backcountry-0002.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R6F-deer-backcountry-0002.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed paved road

evidence.t: No official deer winter range within 500 m, so the top score here is 8 of 11. This score leans on cutblocks, burns, habitat zone and aspect.
Cutblock harvested 2010 (16 years old), right here.
Burn from 2023 (fire VA1638, 3,830 ha), right here.
Habitat zone Coastal Western Hemlock (CWHds2): coast forest, where black tailed deer are among the most common large mammals (95%) and use logged ground often (80%) (lesson: Wet forests).
W facing slope, 40 degrees: sun melts snow first.

seasonRows.notes: LEH (Limited Entry Hunting): draw only, not a general open season
MU 5-9 is not listed in the Region 5 white tailed deer rows (my reading of the table).
